name: High-carbon steel splint vambraces
description: Short canvas forearm guards with strips of high-carbon steel riveted along them, strapped on at the wrist. They fit over mail.
notes: Laid side by side, open side down: each vambrace is a canvas shell curved across the forearm, 120 mm long and 110 mm across, with four steel splints riveted along it between bare canvas strips, leather binding at both ends and one buckled strap. The pair lies side by side with the strap tails out, 316 mm across; each vambrace is 120 mm long. Shares the mild steel pair's model with splints and rivets in `steel-blued`. Slot `arms` follows the earlier clothing batches' arm guards. The xl and xs sizes share the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Mild steel shoulder guards
description: A pair of shoulder guards made of four overlapping curved mild steel plates on a leather strap, made to be buckled onto a brigandine.
notes: Lying crown up side by side: each guard is four overlapping steel lames 150 mm across on a leather strap riveted along their crowns, with a buckle tab at the strap end. The curved lames enclose air. Worn by mounting on a brigandine's shoulder points, so it `fits` `brigandine` and its `wearable` has no slot. Protection and wear follow the mild steel vambraces. The xl and xs sizes share the model.
